stations.name: Kabataş Ferry Terminal
stations.note: The main European-side ferry terminal — directly reachable from Heya via F1 funicular + tram (about 12 min).

destinations.name: Adalar (Büyükada · Heybeliada · Burgazada · Kınalıada)
destinations.duration: 75–105 min (BUDO/Şehir Hatları fast ferries ~75 min, classic ferries ~95 min)
destinations.frequency: Ferries every 1–2 hours, daily ~07:00–22:00 (Şehir Hatları). BUDO and TURYOL add fast-ferry sailings in summer.
destinations.ticket: Istanbulkart (~₺60–80 with card, more at the booth). BUDO ferries are ticketed separately.
destinations.tip: Buy Istanbulkart at any kiosk (₺200 refundable deposit) and load credit. Lines form 15 min before departure.

stations.name: Eminönü Ferry Terminal
stations.note: Historic ferry hub on the Golden Horn — tram T1 stop. Best for the Bosphorus-line ferry to Anadolu Kavağı (Yoros).

destinations.name: Adalar (Büyükada · Heybeliada · Kınalıada · Burgazada)
destinations.duration: 100–120 min (older, slower ferries — but the classic experience)
destinations.frequency: 5–6 sailings per day, daily ~07:00–21:00 (Şehir Hatları only).

destinations.name: Bosphorus line: Anadolu Kavağı (Yoros Castle)
destinations.duration: ~2 h 15 min one way (with stops at Beşiktaş, Rumeli Kavağı)
destinations.frequency: 1–2 sailings per day each direction, daily in summer (April–October), weekends-only in winter.
destinations.tip: The Bosphorus line is one of the great urban ferry rides in the world — passes Dolmabahçe, Çırağan, the two Bosphorus bridges, Rumeli Hisarı, and the Bosphorus-Black Sea meeting point.

destinations.name: Kadıköy · Üsküdar (Asian side, across the Bosphorus)

stations.name: Beşiktaş Ferry Terminal
stations.note: Bosphorus-side terminal — served by the Bosphorus line (toward Yoros) and short hops to Üsküdar.

destinations.name: Anadolu Kavağı (Yoros Castle) — Bosphorus line
destinations.duration: ~1 h 45 min one way from Beşiktaş

stations.name: Kadıköy Ferry Terminal
stations.note: The main Asian-side ferry terminal — across from Eminönü. Backs onto the Kadıköy market and Bağdat Avenue.

stations.name: Üsküdar Ferry Terminal
stations.note: Best Asian-side access to the Old City (Eminönü via ferry is faster than metro through the tunnels).

stations.name: Bostancı Ferry Terminal
stations.note: Asian-side fast-ferry terminal to the islands. Farther out than Kadıköy but the boats are quicker.

destinations.name: Adalar (Büyükada · Heybeliada · Kınalıada · Burgazada)
destinations.duration: 45–60 min (faster than Kabataş, since less of the Bosphorus to cover)
destinations.frequency: Several daily sailings, mostly spring–autumn. Reduced schedule in winter.

stations.name: Anadolu Kavağı Pier
stations.note: Terminus of the Bosphorus line, at the Black Sea mouth. Gateway to Yoros Castle (20 min walk uphill).

destinations.name: Eminönü · Beşiktaş (return Bosphorus line, European side)
destinations.frequency: 1–2 return sailings per day, summer schedule (April–October).

stations.name: Büyükada Pier
stations.note: Main pier on the largest of the Princes' Islands. Phaeton (horse-carriage) and bicycle rentals here.

stations.name: Heybeliada Pier
stations.note: Main pier on the greenest of the islands, with views of Halki Theological School across the bay.

stations.name: Burgazada Pier
stations.note: Smallest pier of the four main islands — quiet, with a calm waterfront and Sait Faik's house up the hill.

notes: Schedules above are general guidance. Always check the day-of at the official Şehir Hatları site (sehirhatlari.istanbul) or app — frequencies change by season, weather, and weekday vs weekend.
Istanbulkart is the reloadable transport card that works on all ferries, metros, trams, and buses. Get one at any kiosk (₺200 refundable deposit) and load credit.
The Bosphorus line from Eminönü to Anadolu Kavağı (Yoros Castle) is one of the great urban ferry rides in the world — it's how most Istanbulites first fall in love with the city.
